correctness.rationale: The Kanenobu–Kazama presentation gives \(\phi(A)=B\), \(\phi(B)=A^{-1}B\) in the class-two Heisenberg group and fixes \(C=[A,B]\); direct iteration has period six. The meridional quotient is the coinvariant quotient by \(\phi^n(g)g^{-1}\), so only \(n\bmod6\) matters. Residues 1 and 5 kill \(A,B,C\); residues 2 and 4 force \(B=A^2\), then \(C=1\) and \(A^3=1\), leaving \(C_{\gcd(k,3)}\); residue 3 gives \(A^2=B^2=C^{-1}\), and centrality yields \(C^2=1\), so odd \(k\) forces the whole kernel trivial. Residue 0 retains \(H_k\). On the surviving \(C_3\), \(\phi(A)=A^{-1}\), producing the stated semidirect product. The inspected finite normal-closure checker agrees for representative odd moduli but is not used as the proof.
